name: QAGOMA
funding: 1.17M visits (2024-25); Queensland Government statutory body; Creative Australia, Shayher Group, Carnival Cruise Line, Tim Fairfax Family Foundation.
watch: Carnival Corporation, parent of Carnival Cruise Line, paid $40M for oily-waste dumping in 2016 and $20M in 2019 for probation violations.
records_note: Publishes statutory annual reports with financial statements and trustees back to 1991-92; the main site blocked checks of its donor pages.

name: Queens Museum
funding: City-owned building. Public funds from NYC Department of Cultural Affairs, NY State Council on the Arts, the state legislature, the Queens Borough President and City Council; foundations and members.
watch: In 2017 the museum cancelled, then reinstated, an Israeli UN event after backlash. In October 2023 staff sent a letter and struck over Palestine.
records_note: Names its public funders with no date and lists its trustees; no annual report on the site, Form 990s for 2001 to 2025 on ProPublica.

name: RAK Art Foundation
funding: Al Qasimi Foundation, primarily funded by the Ruler of Ras Al Khaimah.

name: Recess
funding: New York State Council on the Arts (NYSCA), NYC Department of Cultural Affairs (DCLA), Andy Warhol Foundation; 501(c)(3) non-profit.

name: REDCAT (Roy and Edna Disney/CalArts Theater)
funding: California Institute of the Arts (CalArts), National Endowment for the Arts, LA County Department of Arts and Culture; non-profit.

name: Remai Modern
funding: C$13.1M revenue in 2025, 51% from City of Saskatoon grants. Sponsors include the Frank and Ellen Remai Foundation, SaskEnergy, SIGA, SaskTel, SGI and TD.
watch: SaskEnergy, Cameco uranium, Sask Lotteries. 2019 board upheaval.
records_note: It posts reports for 2016 to 2025 with a 2025 donor list and its board, but audited accounts are available only on request.

name: Rencontres de Bamako
funding: Mali's Ministry of Culture organises and the Institut français co-produces. Royal Air Maroc is a long-time partner. No full funder list is published.
watch: African photography biennale since 1994. The 15th edition runs 26 November 2026 to 26 January 2027. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: The festival site names its 2026 partners, led by Mali's culture ministry, with earlier editions filterable, but posts no reports, accounts or board.

name: Reykjavík Art Museum
funding: Municipal museum funded by the City of Reykjavík.
records_note: Posts its 2023 annual report; its parent City of Reykjavik posts consolidated annual accounts. No sponsor list, and no current board for the museum.

name: RiddoDuottarMuseat
funding: 2023: about NOK 15M in public operating grants, NOK 13.1M of it from the Sámi Parliament (Sametinget), plus Finnmark county and four municipalities.
watch: A Sámi museum foundation running several sites.
records_note: RDM posts annual reports for 2014 to 2025 and names its eight board members, but no donor list; its accounts are in Norway's register.

name: Riwaq Biennale
funding: Riwaq NGO: EU, Sweden, Germany/KfW, UNDP, UNESCO, ALIPH, British Council CPF, Ford, Open Society, Prince Claus, Doen, Arab Fund, OPEC Fund.
watch: OPEC Fund for International Development (oil-state money) is on Riwaq's donor list. Last full biennale 2014; 2019 Chicago edition.
records_note: Riwaq posts annual reports for 2010 to 2025, an auditor's report in 2025, an undated named donor list, and its board in each report.

name: Rockbund Art Museum
funding: Private museum in the Rockbund development on the Bund. Current credits name the Octone Foundation and ROCKBUND; no funder list or budget is published.
watch: Non-profit contemporary museum located in the historic Royal Asiatic Society building in Shanghai. Governed under Shanghai Civil Affairs Bureau non-profit regulations with curatorial independence.
records_note: Its support page names founders Lynn and Thomas Ou and lead sponsors Rockbund and Ping An, undated; no annual report, accounts or board are posted.
